summary: PR #261 (CASSSIDECAR-347) caches the merged map returned by FilteringMetricRegistry.getMetrics() and invalidates it on register, remove and excluded-metric creation. It also precomputes the PeriodicTaskKey hash code and adds a CHANGES.txt entry. Checklist applied: refdir/sidecar/TESTING.md plus the cass-test-regime lens notes in sidecar-standards.md. The right suite is used: plain JUnit unit tests in FilteringMetricRegistryTest need no Cassandra, so no integration test is required. This is a performance improvement, not a bug fix, so a test that fails on base is not expected; the new tests check that invalidation keeps results correct. The main gap is that the concurrency tests would not fail on a thread-side assertion failure, and none of them runs getMetrics() concurrently with removal or with excluded-metric creation, which is the racy interleaving. Not reviewed: nothing.

findings.title: Surface failures from worker threads in the concurrent registration test
findings.rule: Test must be able to fail; assertions check the outcome
findings.problem: pool.submit(...) at line 338 discards the returned Future. The assertThat(registry.getMetrics()).isNotEmpty() on line 346 runs inside the task, so an AssertionError or any other exception there is swallowed by the executor and the test still passes. The assertion is also trivially true, because the calling thread has just registered a metric. The test therefore does not check what getMetrics() returns while registrations are in flight. The only real check is the single getMetrics() call after awaitTermination.
findings.fix: Collect the Futures and call get() on each, or record the Throwables in a queue and assert it is empty. Replace isNotEmpty() with an assertion that can fail under a race, for example that the map contains the metric this thread just registered.

findings.title: Interleave getMetrics reads with writers in the concurrency tests
findings.rule: Coverage of the change; timing-sensitive tests need evidence of repeated runs
findings.problem: The cache is invalidated in addExcludedMetricIfNotExists before the metric is inserted into excludedMetrics, and in register/remove only after the mutation. In the removal test (line 374) getMetrics() is called only before the threads start and after they finish, never concurrently with remove(). In the registration test each thread calls getMetrics() once, right after its own register(). A stale cache, for example one that misses an excluded metric because getMetrics() ran between the invalidation and the insert, would only show up as a lost or extra entry in the final call, and only in a rare interleaving. The test would almost always pass against a faulty invalidation order. Nothing in the PR shows repeated runs, and the 100-thread, latch-released tests are timing-sensitive.
findings.fix: Add a reader thread that loops on getMetrics() while writers register and remove. After all writers finish, assert the final map equals the expected key set. Run the test in a repeated loop (for example @RepeatedTest) or show repeated-run evidence in the PR.

findings.title: Assert remove() return values and the cache refresh after removal
findings.rule: Coverage of the change: new branches and boundaries are exercised
findings.problem: remove() was rewritten with two branches: excluded metric present, or fall back to super.remove(). It also gained a new return-value contract (true if removed). The test discards the return value and asserts only the final map sizes. It never checks that removing a missing name returns false, or that getMetrics() drops a removed excluded or included metric on the very next call. A stale cached map after a single remove() would not be caught on the deterministic path.
findings.fix: Add a deterministic test: register an included and an excluded metric, call getMetrics(), then remove each and assert the return value is true and the next getMetrics() omits it. Assert that removing an unknown name returns false.

findings.title: Assert that getMetrics() returns the cached map between mutations
findings.problem: The point of the change is that getMetrics() returns a precomputed map until the registry changes. No test checks that two consecutive calls with no mutation return the same instance, or that a mutation produces a new one. A regression back to rebuilding the map on every call would pass every new test.
findings.fix: Add assertThat(registry.getMetrics()).isSameAs(registry.getMetrics()) with no mutation in between, and isNotSameAs after a register().
